correctness.rationale: For 0<alpha<1 the strictly positive stable variable with Laplace transform exp(-t^alpha) exists by the integrable Poisson Levy measure. Tonelli and differentiation give E[1/(1+u S/S')]=1/(1+u^alpha). The Stieltjes inversion density is positive, normalized, and integrates to the stated explicit CDF and quantile. Differentiation of the Bernoulli log-MGF then gives the exact fractional-logistic identity. The empirical midpoint parameters converge to this law, so normalized log-MGFs and first two derivatives converge to that of alpha Bin(N,1/2). Chernoff upper bounds and exponential-tilt concentration prove matching one-sided logarithmic tails at every fixed interior threshold. A subsequential quantile contradiction using strict monotonicity of those rates on both sides of the common mean controls all quantile levels, including extremely small ones, and proves W_infinity/N->0. Boundaries alphaN versus floor(alphaN) are handled by the common support [0,alphaN].

originality.rationale: Tang and Tang explicitly ask in arXiv:1908.10024v1, Open Problem 4.6, for a Poisson-binomial approximation to (2/3)Bin(3n,1/2) with W_infinity=o(n). Their fixed-homogeneous and equispaced-heterogeneous proposals fail with linear errors and they offer small-n examples only. Mattner's 2022 MSC-60E15 theorem treats extreme expectations conditional on finitely many moments, not this asymptotic maximal-transport question. The classical Lamperti stable ratio law is used as background, not treated as new. Published-source and semantic published-record searches for fractional Bernoulli logistic mixture, the named problem, and matching Cramer rates found no covering resolution. Remaining priority risk: an equivalent construction may be buried in literature under stable-ratio/large-deviation terminology.
residual_risks: Undiscovered general Lamperti-mixture approximation theorem may imply the same transport result under a different vocabulary.
The original source poses an even stronger bounded-error challenge; this finding does not settle it.

value.rationale: The result directly resolves the sublinear half of a published explicit Poisson-binomial optimal-transport problem. It gives constructive strongly Rayleigh approximants for every fixed real scaling in (0,1), with an exact parameter law, matches the entire strictly convex Cramer rate function rather than merely moments or CLTs, and proves uniform quantile control even at exponential tail levels. The source rules out several natural simpler constructions at the desired scale, so this is a substantively motivated positive theorem.
